record.question: A patient on warfarin should avoid large increases in foods rich in:
record.explanation: Answer A: Vitamin K. Warfarin’s anticoagulant effect can change with major changes in vitamin K intake; patients are generally advised to keep intake consistent rather than eliminate vitamin-K foods. Source/context note: “Avoid” could imply complete avoidance; the recommended advice is consistent intake and clinician/INR monitoring. Reference: https://www.nhs.uk/medicines/warfarin/food-and-drink-while-taking-warfarin/. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.

record.question: Carotenoids such as beta-carotene are important because:
options: They can increase the haemoglobin level
They act as precursors of vitamin A
They can increase the level of vitamin C
They can reduce the side effects of oral iron
record.explanation: Answer B: They act as precursors of vitamin A. Beta-carotene is a provitamin A carotenoid that the body can convert to vitamin A. Reference: https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminA-HealthProfessional/. Verified worked solution, unofficial.
